summary: Comprehensive frontend testing of SwiftResolwe landing page completed via Playwright on the preview URL. 56 distinct UI/interaction/content assertions executed. All MUST-HAVE flows (landing render, all 10 sections + 2 callouts + header + footer, sticky header CTA on scroll>80, smooth-scroll nav, mobile hamburger menu at 414px, hero CTAs to /file-a-dispute and /triage, hero triage SVG diagram, trust metrics 45/90/100 count-up, ticker, 8 placeholder logos, 3 resolution tier cards with verbatim statute citations, 3 panel-of-neutrals categories with Section 12 disclosure, 4-column enterprise verticals with Section 138 NI Act + Section 25 PSS Act, 3-step retail pipeline at #retail, economic-advantage 22x timeline ratio (measured 21.56x), claim slider updates cost-saved+claim-display, FAQ single-open accordion with aria-expanded, footer 4 columns + compliance badges + © 2026 copyright, all three placeholder routes /file-a-dispute /login /triage rendering with shared header/footer and Back-to-Landing link) PASS. All 9 statute strings present VERBATIM. Initial test reported 8 false negatives — all confirmed as test-script artifacts (CSS text-transform:uppercase makes inner_text uppercase; React controlled <input range> required Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor setter; first nav-link scrolled correctly but check timed at 900ms — at 2500ms it lands at top:-0.07). No real functional or content bugs found.

issues: Triage diagram (data-testid='hero-diagram') output-tier badge cards on the right edge (TIER 01 Negotiate / TIER 02 Mediate / TIER 03 Arbitrate) are visually clipped by the diagram container — labels render as 'Negotia', 'Mediat', 'Arbitrat' because the right edge of each card extends past the SVG/card bounding box. Either widen the container, shrink the label font, or shift the output nodes inward (~24px) so the full word is visible.

action_items: (Polish, non-blocking) Fix Triage diagram label clipping on the right edge so 'Negotiate', 'Mediate', 'Arbitrate' render fully inside the hero diagram card.

(Optional) Footer compliance badges and the 'Coming Soon · Form Placeholder' label render uppercase via CSS text-transform — visually correct but if any downstream test checks the raw cased string via inner_text it will see uppercase. Just an awareness note for future automation.
critical_code_review_comments: Landing.jsx renders ScrollProgress + Header + 10 sections + Footer cleanly with stable id anchors (#retail, #enterprise, #tiers, #panel, #economics, #faq) matching the header nav links.
Header.jsx: smooth-scroll uses scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'}) — works; AnimatePresence reveal of header-file-dispute at scrollY>80 is correctly gated.
EconomicAdvantage.jsx: timeline true-22x scale implemented as widthPct={97} (court) vs {4.5} (odr) → measured DOM ratio 21.56× ≈ exact intent. Solid.

ResolutionTiers.jsx, EnterpriseVerticals.jsx, PanelOfNeutrals.jsx, FAQTerminal.jsx: every legally-sensitive statute string ('Section 10A of the Information Technology Act, 2000', 'Section 85/63 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023', 'Section 27 of the Mediation Act, 2023', 'Section 36/12 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996', 'Section 31A of the Arbitration Act', 'Section 138 (NI Act)', 'Section 25 (PSS Act)') is hardcoded verbatim and verified in DOM.
FAQTerminal.jsx: single-open accordion logic (openIdx state with -1 sentinel) is correct; aria-expanded toggles properly.
Hero.jsx triage diagram: minor visual polish needed — three right-side output badges overflow the diagram container at lg breakpoint.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Frontend-only marketing site. All flows verified PASS. The ONLY observable issue is cosmetic clipping of the three right-side tier labels inside the hero TriageDiagram at >=lg viewports. When writing future Playwright tests against this site: (a) for the claim-slider use Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype,'value').set + dispatch 'input' event, a plain el.value=... will not propagate to React state; (b) body.inner_text() reflects CSS uppercase — assert case-insensitively for footer badges and the 'Coming Soon · Form Placeholder' label; (c) allow >=2s wait after clicking a smooth-scroll nav link before measuring getBoundingClientRect. data-testid coverage is excellent across header, hero, all 10 sections, FAQ rows, calculator, timeline, footer, and placeholder routes.
rca of the issue: No production bugs found. The only follow-up is the cosmetic Triage diagram label clipping on desktop. Likely cause: the output-tier badges are absolutely-positioned with x-offsets close to the SVG/container right edge; either reduce padding on each badge, reduce font-size from text-sm to text-xs, or shift x-coordinate of the three output nodes left by ~24-32px so labels stay inside the card.
